partners.diseaseBName: combined immunodeficiency due to ZAP70 deficiency

#### 1. combined immunodeficiency due to ZAP70 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.477)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-202433)

**Proposed mechanism:** ZAP70 (HGNC:12700) —DISRUPTS→ T-cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP492); T-cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP492) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired T-cell function (HP:0005364); Impaired T-cell function (HP:0005364) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0001912); CD3E (HGNC:2357) —DISRUPTS→ T-cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP492). Loss-of-function mutations in ZAP70 disrupt the T-cell receptor signaling pathway, leading to impaired T-cell function and combined immunodeficiency. Similarly, defects in CD3E, a component of the T-cell receptor complex, also disrupt T-cell receptor signaling, converging on the same downstream pathway and resulting in similar immunodeficiency phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of pathogenic variants in ZAP70 or CD3E in individuals with combined immunodeficiency would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if a significant proportion of patients with combined immunodeficiency and these specific phenotypes do not carry variants in either ZAP70 or CD3E, or if experimental evidence shows distinct downstream pathway disruptions, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing a high frequency (>1%) of potentially pathogenic variants in ZAP70 or CD3E in the general population would suggest these genes are not the primary drivers of rare combined immunodeficiency.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared T-cell receptor signaling pathway defect in ZAP70 deficiency and CD3E deficiency highlights potential therapeutic targets for immune reconstitution strategies, such as gene therapy or targeted immunomodulation, aiming to restore T-cell function.
